title: Serving runtime ops — contraflow weekly (kernel / KV / batching)
content:
Weekly standup notes: contraflow experiment week
Date: 2027-04-11
Attendees: Sofia Li (chair), Marco Ruiz, Aisha Patel, Jun Park, Diego Morales, ops-oncall

Purpose: capture operational observations from the 'contraflow' run (reversed prioritization for micro-batching), surface kernel regressions seen during shadow runs, and decide next steps for KV warmup and batching heuristics. This is intentionally informal — raw triage and action items.

High-level summary:
- Ran contraflow scheduling for 48h across two clusters (us-west-2 prod-like and dev-gpu-02). Observed 9% median P50 token-latency improvement for long-context chat (>= 1024) at steady load. Tail (P99) saw mixed signals: improved on us-west-2 but regressed 18% on dev-gpu-02 under synthetic burst tests.
- KV cache warmup (shadow-warmup) improved prefix hit rate from 62% -> 78% for targeted workload cohort A (search-rewrite flows) after changing prefetch window to 8 tokens.
- Kernel scheduling races surfaced on PR #842; allocator backpressure path can deadlock when microkernel-preempt and contraflow both enabled.

Detailed observations:
1) Contraflow scheduling effects
   - Behavior: reversing batch priority (older requests get starved last) improved batching aggregation for long-context by grouping longer sessions together. Reduced kernel context-switch overhead.
   - Metrics (us-west-2): P50 token latency -9%, throughput +4% at 90th percentile load.
   - Metrics (dev-gpu-02): P99 token latency +18% during synthetic burst (spike pattern B: 400 rps->1600 rps in 6s). Investigation points to allocator thrash when many small chat sessions suddenly ramp.

2) Kernel race / allocator issue
   - Symptom: intermittent stalls (10-30s) on worker threads, stack traces show waiting on allocator queue while preempting microkernel contexts.
   - Repro: locally with stress harness (ticket JIRA-4132) using PR #842 applied, with microkernel-preempt enabled.
   - Temporary mitigation: disable microkernel-preempt on prod clusters until patch merged. Ops applied rollback on nodes in us-west-2 Canary pool 2 at 2027-04-13 03:10 UTC.

3) KV cache warmup & shadow-warmup
   - Change: increased prefetch window from 4->8 tokens for cohort A and enabled shadow-warmup to populate cold nodes.
   - Result: prefix hit rate improvement 62%->78% within 2h for traffic mirrored to staging; reduced cold-start tokens by ~27K tokens/min during ramp.
   - Caveat: memory pressure increased on small-instance pools by ~6%. Need eviction tuning for microstate caches.

4) Batching heuristics adjustments
   - Introduced a soft-timeout (10ms -> 8ms) for coalescer for requests tagged long-context to encourage grouping. This cut intra-batch variance but increased average batch size modestly.
   - Observed more consistent KV cache reuse across batch members.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Is the contraflow approach tactical (workaround for current kernel costs) or strategic? If strategic, we should build a mode flag and safety limits.
- Memory increase from shadow-warmup: can we implement a per-pool warmup throttle to avoid small-instance OOMs?
- How do we instrument allocator queues to get meaningful SLO alarms instead of the current coarse CPU/RAM thresholds?

Action items (owners + target dates):
- Marco: triage allocator deadlock and draft a non-blocking allocator fallback. Patch due EOD 2027-04-16. (linked PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/859)
- Aisha: run extended contraflow A/B on us-west-2 Canary pool for another week (target end 2027-04-18); capture P50/P90/P99 and memory impact.
- Jun: implement per-pool warmup throttle and add metrics for warmup memory delta. Prototype by 2027-04-20.
- Diego: update oncall runbook to include rollback steps for microkernel-preempt and contraflow interactions; provide checklist and K8s labels to use. Due 2027-04-14.
- Sofia: coordinate a brief design doc outlining whether contraflow becomes a config toggle surfaced in Console. Draft by 2027-04-22.

Notes from ops/incident side:
- Incident observed 2027-04-12 22:43 UTC affecting dev-gpu-02; cause traced to combined stress test + microkernel-preempt. Postmortem entry created (JIRA-4139).
- Canary rollback timeline captured in slack thread #serving-runtime-ops (link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/CRUNTIME/conv1234).

Helpful logs / quick findings:
- Sample stack trace snippet (sanitized) attached in PR #842 comments. Shows allocator wait path and preempt queue interplay.
- Heap delta per pod (before/after shadow-warmup) attached to Confluence note.

Decisions made:
- Rollback microkernel-preempt by default on small-instance pools until allocator fallback in place.
- Continue contraflow experiments on canary with memory guardrails.

Risks / next blockers:
- If allocator fallback patch slips beyond next week, we risk recurring P99 regressions during peak bursts in dev clusters.
- Memory pressure could surface on customer-dedicated small-GPU pools; need to proactively add warmup throttle.

Follow-ups for next standup (2027-04-18):
- Marco to present allocator fallback design and demo simple benchmark.
- Aisha to present updated canary metrics and memory trends.
- Jun to share early telemetry from warmup throttle in staging.

Misc notes / brain dump:
- Consider renaming 'contraflow' to something less ambiguous if it graduates (ideas: 'long-session-coalescer', 'session-affinity-batcher').
- There's an odd correlation between anti-entropy sync windows and contraflow efficiency — need to verify if periodic syncs are perturbing batch alignment.

End of notes.
